reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but the server handlers independently compose the daily skip-versus-shift policy already implemented in getNextDate.

duplication.why: Daily non-working-day filtering and conditional shifting are repeated across getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: Holiday matching and date movement remain in shared/schedules.ts, but the server handlers also own scheduling policy that belongs alongside those shared definitions.

scope.why: The edits are focused on the requested scheduling rules, range handler, configuration plumbing, and supporting tests.

maintainability.why: The helpers are understandable, but maintaining several occurrence-processing pipelines with separate search bounds and policy composition increases the cost of future rule changes.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange enumerate raw RSchedule occurrences and reproduce daily filtering and adjustment dispatch instead of sharing the occurrence policy implemented in getNextDate.

disguised_duplication.where: The same daily exclusion decision appears as candidates.find in getNextWeekdayOccurrence, an array filter in getUpcomingDates, and a continue branch in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: Holiday support adds a holidays argument to getDateWithSkippedWeekend and a holidays option to WeekendRule; getNextDate gains a daily-specific branch, while getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange independently implement the skip-versus-shift pipeline.
